record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: Can exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic systems be tuned by external stimuli such as electric field or strain?

evidence.quote: xii. Can the EB effect be tuned by external stimuli (electrical field, strain) in vdW magnetic systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a magnetic heterostructure formed by stacking two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic layers (for instance, a ferromagnet/antiferromagnet bilayer such as Fe3GeTe2/FePS3 or CrCl3/Fe3GeTe2). After field-cooling, such a heterostructure can exhibit the exchange-bias effect: the hysteresis loop of the magnetization M(H) is shifted along the magnetic-field axis by an amount H_EB = -(H_+ + H_-)/2, where H_+ and H_- denote the positive and negative coercive fields. Determine whether, and by what microscopic mechanisms, the exchange-bias field H_EB (and the associated blocking temperature T_B) in such two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic heterostructures can be continuously and reversibly tuned by external stimuli, specifically (i) an applied electric field or electrostatic/ionic gating and (ii) mechanical strain or hydrostatic pressure that modifies the interlayer van der Waals spacing.
artifact.category_tag: Exchange bias in 2D van der Waals magnets
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent experimental work demonstrates that exchange bias in 2D van der Waals heterostructures can indeed be tuned by both external stimuli mentioned. Electric/gate control was shown in FePS3–Fe5GeTe2 (protonic gating, Nano Letters 2022; arXiv:2203.10686) and in MnBi2Te4/Cr2Ge2Te6. Strain/pressure tuning of H_EB and T_B has been reported in FePSe3/Fe3GeTe2 via pressure engineering of the vdW spacing. A complete microscopic understanding (e.g. quantitative theory linking interface exchange coupling, anisotropy, and uncompensated spins to gate voltage or strain) is still under active investigation, so the broader question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Electric Control of Exchange Bias Effect in FePS3–Fe5GeTe2 van der Waals Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: By applying a solid protonic gate, the EB effects were repeatably electrically tuned in FePS3-Fe5GeTe2.
status_evidence.claim: Electric-field/gate tuning of exchange bias in a vdW heterostructure has been demonstrated experimentally.

status_evidence.title: Gate-tunable exchange bias effect in FePS3-Fe5GeTe2 van der Waals heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Gate-tunable exchange bias effect reported in FePS3-Fe5GeTe2 vdW heterostructures.
status_evidence.claim: Gate tunability of EB is confirmed in a 2D vdW system.

status_evidence.title: Manipulating exchange bias in 2D magnetic heterojunction for high-performance robust memory applications
status_evidence.snippet: Manipulation of exchange bias in 2D magnetic heterojunctions.
status_evidence.claim: Active research program continues to manipulate EB in 2D vdW magnets.
